candidates.title: Tailoring the Quantization Space for 1-Bit KV Cache Compression
candidates.abstract: The key-value (KV) cache becomes a major memory bottleneck in long-context LLM inference, placing substantial pressure on memory capacity and bandwidth. To mitigate this bottleneck, vector quantization (VQ) has emerged as a promising approach for aggressive KV cache compression. However, existing VQ methods degrade substantially in the 1-bit regime. At such extreme compression, each codebook must represent a larger group of channels with a limited set of centroids, making effective use of its capacity increasingly challenging. To address this, we introduce $\textbf{TaSQ}$, which tailors the VQ target space by combining query-guided channel weighting, cross-head normalization, and covariance-aware channel grouping to better reflect the error sensitivity and statistical structure of cached activations. Since these transforms are RoPE-compatible and can be easily merged into projection weights and codebooks, TaSQ preserves the conventional VQ lookup structure and adds negligible serving overhead. Across general, long-chain-of-thought reasoning, and long-context retrieval benchmarks, TaSQ consistently outperforms existing low-bit KV cache VQ baselines while preserving reasoning stability. On a single RTX 6000 Ada GPU, its SGLang implementation supports up to $14\times$ larger batch sizes and achieves $1.87\times$ higher peak throughput compared to the BF16 baseline.
candidates.reason: KV cacheの1-bit vector quantizationでcentroid数が不足する問題に対し、query誘導のchannel重み、head間正規化、共分散を考慮したchannel groupingで量子化空間を整えるTaSQを提案する。RoPE互換の変換をprojection重みとcodebookへ吸収し、従来VQ lookupの構造を保つ。著者要旨はRTX6000 Ada/SGLang実装でBF16比batch最大14倍、ピークthroughput1.87倍を報告。KV圧縮と推論servingへの直接的貢献としてaccept。

candidates.title: LIRQuant: An Efficient Locally Isolated Rotation Quantization Method for Large Language Models
candidates.venue: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
candidates.abstract: Post-Training Quantization (PTQ) enables efficient deployment of Large Language Models (LLMs), yet activation outliers remain a key challenge for low-bit quantization. Existing global transformation methods overlook heterogeneous channel sensitivity to quantization noise, leading to suboptimal accuracy-efficiency trade-offs. To address this, we propose \textbf{Locally Isolated Rotation Quantization (LIRQuant)}, a sensitivity-aware framework that selectively applies transformations. LIRQuant identifies sensitive channels using a noise-weighted sensitivity metric, applying expressive learnable rotations only to these channels and lightweight fixed rotations to the remaining ones. This decoupled design reduces optimization complexity without sacrificing outlier smoothing capability. Extensive experiments across the LLaMA-2/3, Mistral, Qwen3, and Mixtral families demonstrate that LIRQuant achieves state-of-the-art accuracy under the challenging W4A4KV4 setting. Meanwhile, LIRQuant calibrates LLaMA-3-8B in only 25 minutes with 20.3 GB peak GPU memory, achieving the fastest calibration and the lowest memory footprint among recent learnable-rotation methods, and its fused inference kernels deliver up to $2.3\times$ prefill speedup and $3.5\times$ memory saving over FP16.

priority_breakdown.matched_prestigious_venue: Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing

candidates.reason: W4A4KV4など低ビット推論のactivation outlierに対し、感度の高いチャネルだけ学習可能な回転、残りは軽量な固定回転を適用する局所分離型PTQを提案する。著者要旨はLlama3-8Bの較正25分、ピークGPUメモリ20.3GB、fused inference kernelによるFP16比prefill最大2.3倍、メモリ3.5倍削減を報告。推論圧縮と実行kernelへの明確な適用があるためaccept。

candidates.title: AlignQuant: Tile-Aligned Mixed-Precision Quantization for Efficient LLM Generation
candidates.abstract: Fine-grained mixed-precision quantization promises efficient large language model inference, but local precision choices can conflict with regular GPU storage and computation units. This precision-boundary mismatch limits the translation of compression into practical acceleration. We introduce AlignQuant, a post-training quantization method that uses GPU-compatible two-dimensional weight tiles as the common unit of precision allocation, compact storage, and execution. This shared partition lets precision follow sensitivity within output channels. Joint prefill/decode calibration scores precision reductions using projection-output perturbations weighted by language-model loss gradients under quantized activations. Phase-normalized scores prioritize higher precision for tiles important to either phase under a model-wide weight-storage budget. Each tile stores one selected representation, while phase-specialized kernels reuse the packed model and expand lower-bit weights for INT8 computation with 8-bit activations. Across four LLMs spanning 3B to 14B parameters, AlignQuant achieves up to $2.50\times$ generation speedup over BF16 while preserving model quality. Evaluations further cover three GPUs and contexts up to 64K tokens. These results show that local precision flexibility and regular GPU execution can coexist through a shared tile unit. The implementation is available at https://github.com/HanzhiZhang-Ulrica/AlignQuant.
candidates.reason: GPUで扱いやすい2次元weight tileを精度配分・圧縮格納・実行の共通単位にし、チャネル内の量子化感度差を活かす。prefill/decode両フェーズのgradient重み付き出力摂動で混合精度を較正し、同じpacked weightをINT8計算向けphase別kernelで再利用する。著者要旨は3B～14Bの4モデル・3GPU・最大64K contextでBF16比最大2.50倍の生成速度を報告。量子化とGPU実行形状の共同設計としてaccept。

candidates.title: GPU Goldmines: Tunable WebGPU Kernels for Edge LLM Inference
candidates.abstract: As demand for LLM inference grows and consumer GPUs grow more capable, edge deployment is becoming increasingly attractive. WebGPU is compelling in this setting because it offers cross-platform portability and browser accessibility. However, these same strengths also make high performance difficult to achieve, as an implementation that performs well in one context may not perform well in another. To address this, we present GPU Goldmines, a framework for specifying, executing, and tuning WebGPU kernels. We instantiate GPU Goldmines with kernels for key LLM building blocks: matrix multiplication, matrix-vector multiplication, and flash attention. We characterize performance across diverse devices, shapes, and browsers, and use the resulting database to accelerate subsequent autotuning and configuration selection. On shapes drawn from Llama and Qwen models, our matrix multiplication kernels outperform ONNX Runtime and llama.cpp WebGPU kernels by 7.0x and 1.41x geometric mean, respectively, and deliver end-to-end improvements of 1.48x in the prefill stage of llama.cpp for chat workloads.
candidates.reason: WebGPUのブラウザ/端末間でkernel性能が変わる問題に対し、GEMM、GEMV、flash attentionの実装指定・実行・autotuningと、過去の形状・デバイス別測定DBを組み合わせる。著者要旨ではLlama/Qwen形状でONNX Runtime比7.0倍、llama.cpp WebGPU kernel比1.41倍の幾何平均GEMM性能、llama.cppのchat prefillで1.48倍のend-to-end改善を報告。端末内LLM推論kernel最適化としてaccept。

candidates.title: Range: Decoupling KV-Cache Reuse Granularity from Storage Work
candidates.abstract: LLM serving reuses cached key-value (KV) state to skip prefill, and growing contexts push that state past GPU HBM and CPU DRAM onto NVMe SSDs, placing prefix restore on the critical path of time-to-first-token (TTFT). We find that on a well-configured host-issued path the SSD is not the bottleneck: restoring the same 6 GiB of KV takes 2.1 s as 192 objects but 3.0 s as 6,144 objects, and more under layerwise loading, because every layer of the storage stack - lookup, allocation, I/O submission, GPU delivery, store, index - charges per logical object while the bytes stay the same. This cost grows with the KV footprint: longer contexts, deeper models under layerwise loading, and tensor parallelism each multiply the object count. Prior systems move this per-object work from the CPU to the GPU; the work remains per object. This paper presents Range, a KV-cache storage engine for vLLM and LMCache built on one principle: every cost on the storage path scales with bytes or physical batches, never with logical objects. Range tickets replace per-key lookup and ownership with token metadata and physical leases; byte stripes make the on-media layout independent of reuse granularity; completion-owned GPU transfer banks batch delivery and extraction and release each layer to attention as it lands. Range keeps the kernel cuFile path and changes four lines of vLLM. On a fixed 6 GiB restore, Range's median TTFT stays at 1.79-1.80 s across a 32x range of object counts and under layerwise delivery, within 70 ms of the prefix already being resident in GPU memory, while tuned in-process LMCache rises from 2.12 s to 3.01 s. Range improves on the fastest multiprocess DRAM-bounced path by 0.44 s at coarse granularity while moving no payload through host memory, and holds layerwise reuse at the cost of coarse-grained reuse, where the best stock path takes 2.24 s.
candidates.reason: KV接頭部の細粒度再利用がstorage object数に比例するlookup、I/O発行、GPU搬送等の制御費用を生む問題に対し、Range ticketとbyte stripe、GPU transfer bankで物理バッチ処理量にのみ費用が比例するよう設計する。vLLM/LMCacheへ組込み、著者要旨は6GiB復元でobject数32倍変化に対しTTFTを1.79～1.80秒へ維持、従来LMCacheは2.12→3.01秒と報告。KV offloadとSSD階層の直接的実装研究としてaccept。
